title.zh: 卷一百二十六 志第七十九 樂一
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 志第七十九 樂一 Volume 126 Treatises 79: Music 1

sentences.zh: 有宋之樂，自建隆訖崇寧，凡六改作。

translations.literal: The music of Song, from Jianlong through Chongning, was reformed six times in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jianlong era to Chongning, Song court music underwent six major reforms.

sentences.zh: 始，太祖以雅樂聲高，不合中和，乃詔和峴以王朴律準較洛陽銅望臬石尺為新度，以定律呂，故建隆以來有和峴樂。

translations.literal: At the outset, because Taizu held that the pitch of elegant music was too high and did not accord with central harmony, he ordered He Xian to take Wang Pu's pitch standard and compare it with the bronze pitch tube and stone pitch measure at Luoyang to establish new dimensions, thereby fixing the pitch pipes; hence from Jianlong onward there was the music of He Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Emperor Taizu judged that ceremonial music was pitched too high to achieve proper tonal balance. He directed He Xian to calibrate Wang Pu's pitch pipes against the bronze pitch tube and stone standard at Luoyang, set a new scale, and regulate the pitch pipes—giving rise to what came to be known as He Xian's music from the Jianlong reign onward.

sentences.zh: 仁宗留意音律，判太常燕肅言器久不諧，復以朴準考正。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong paid attention to pitch and mode; Yan Su, who was acting as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, said the instruments had long been out of tune and again used Pu's standard to examine and correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong took a keen interest in pitch regulation. Yan Su, acting head of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, reported that the instruments had long been out of tune and proposed recalibrating them against Wang Pu's standard.

sentences.zh: 時李照以知音聞，謂朴準高五律，與古制殊，請依神瞽法鑄編鍾。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhao was known for understanding music; he said Pu's standard was five tones too high and differed from the ancient system, and requested that chime-bells be cast according to the method of the Divine Blind Musician.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao, renowned for his musical expertise, argued that Wang Pu's standard was five tones too high and diverged from ancient practice. He petitioned to cast a set of chime-bells using the method attributed to the Divine Blind Musician.

sentences.zh: 既成，遂請改定雅樂，乃下三律，鍊白石為磬，範中金為鍾，圖三辰、五靈為器之飾，故景祐中有李照樂。

translations.literal: Once they were completed, he then requested reform of elegant music; the pitch was lowered by three tones, white stone was refined into sounding-stones, and gold was cast into bells, with the Three Celestial Bodies and Five Auspicious Creatures depicted as ornament on the instruments; hence in the Jingyou era there was the music of Li Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the bells were finished, he petitioned to overhaul ceremonial music: the pitch was lowered three tones, white stone was worked into sounding-stones, and gold was cast into bells ornamented with the Three Celestial Bodies and Five Auspicious Creatures. Thus the Jingyou era saw what became known as Li Zhao's music.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諫官、御史交論其非，竟復舊制。

translations.literal: Before long, remonstrating officials and censors in succession debated its errors, and in the end the former system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, remonstrating officials and censors joined in criticizing the reform, and the court eventually reverted to the old system.

sentences.zh: 其後詔侍從、禮官參定聲律，阮逸、胡瑗實預其事，更造鍾磬，止下一律，樂名大安。

translations.literal: Afterward an edict ordered attendant officials and ritual officers jointly to fix pitch and mode; Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan actually took part in the affair, remade bells and stones, lowered the pitch by only one tone, and the music was named Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered attendant officials and ritual specialists to settle the pitch standards. Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan took part in the work, had new bells and sounding-stones made, lowered the pitch by a single tone, and named the resulting music Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 乃試考擊，鍾聲弇鬱震掉，不和滋甚，遂獨用之常祀、朝會焉，故皇祐中有阮逸樂。

translations.literal: They then tested it by striking; the bell tones were muffled, depressed, and trembling, and the dissonance grew worse, so it was used alone for regular sacrifices and court assemblies; hence in the Huangyou era there was the music of Ruan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Trial performances showed the bells sounding muffled, dull, and unstable, with disharmony worse than before. The new set was therefore restricted to routine sacrifices and court assemblies, giving rise in the Huangyou era to what was called Ruan Yi's music.

sentences.zh: 神宗御歷，嗣守成憲，未遑制作，間從言者緒正一二。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, he inherited and maintained established institutions and had no leisure for new productions; occasionally he followed those who spoke out and made one or two preliminary corrections.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong came to the throne, he upheld established institutions and had little time for musical reform, though he occasionally adopted suggestions for minor corrections.

sentences.zh: 知禮院楊傑條上舊樂之失，召范鎮、劉几與傑參議。

translations.literal: Yang Jie of the Office for Understanding Ritual submitted in detail the errors of the old music; Fan Zhen and Liu Ji were summoned to deliberate with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jie of the Office for Understanding Ritual submitted a detailed critique of the defects in the existing music. Fan Zhen and Liu Ji were summoned to deliberate with him.

sentences.zh: 几、傑請遵祖訓，一切下王朴樂二律，用仁宗時所制編鍾，追考成周分樂之序，辨正二舞容節；

translations.literal: Ji and Jie requested to follow the ancestral instruction, lower Wang Pu's music altogether by two tones, use the set of chime-bells made in Renzong's time, investigate and restore the order of divided music from the perfected Zhou, and rectify the postures and beats of the two dances;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and Yang Jie urged adherence to ancestral precedent: lower the pitch of Wang Pu's music by two tones overall, use the chime-bells cast in Emperor Renzong's reign, reconstruct the Zhou-era arrangement of ceremonial music, and correct the choreography of the civil and military dances;

sentences.zh: 而鎮欲求一稃二米真黍，以律生尺，改修鍾量，廢四清聲。

translations.literal: But Zhen wished to seek true millet of one part husk to two parts grain, use the pitch pipes to generate the foot-measure, revise bell dimensions, and abolish the four clear tones.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen, by contrast, sought authentic millet with the one-husk-to-two-grain ratio, wished to derive the measuring foot from the pitch pipes, revise bell dimensions accordingly, and abolish the four supplementary clear tones.

sentences.zh: 詔悉從几、傑議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Ji's and Jie's proposals be followed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted Liu Ji and Yang Jie's proposals in full.

sentences.zh: 樂成，奏之郊廟，故元豐中有楊傑、劉几樂。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, it was performed at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; hence in the Yuanfeng era there was the music of Yang Jie and Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When the new music was finished, it was performed at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, giving rise in the Yuanfeng era to what was called the music of Yang Jie and Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 范鎮言其聲雜鄭、?，請太府銅制律造樂。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen said its tones were mixed with Zheng and Wei music and requested that music be made with pitch pipes cast from copper by the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen argued that its tones were tainted with the licentious music of Zheng and Wei, and petitioned to have new music made using pitch pipes cast in copper by the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 哲宗嗣位，以樂來上，按試於庭，比李照樂下一律，故元祐中有范鎮樂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong succeeded to the throne, Zhen presented his music; it was tested in the courtyard and was found one tone lower than Li Zhao's music; hence in the Yuanyou era there was the music of Fan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong succeeded to the throne, Fan Zhen presented his music for trial in the palace courtyard. It proved one tone lower than Li Zhao's system, giving rise in the Yuanyou era to what was called Fan Zhen's music.

sentences.zh: 楊傑復議其失，謂出於鎮一家之學，卒置不用。

translations.literal: Yang Jie again debated its errors, saying it sprang from the learning of Zhen's family alone, and in the end it was set aside and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jie again criticized its flaws, arguing that it rested on Fan Zhen's private theories alone, and the court ultimately set it aside.

sentences.zh: 徽宗銳意制作，以文太平，於是蔡京主魏漢津之說，破先儒累黍之非，用夏禹以身為度之文，以帝指為律度，鑄帝鼐、景鍾。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong was keen to create new productions and adorn the age with culture; thereupon Cai Jing championed the views of Wei Hanjin, refuted the errors of the former Confucians' stacked-millet method, used the text about Yu of Xia taking the body as measure, took the emperor's finger as pitch standard, and cast the Imperial Cauldron and the Splendid Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong was determined to create new ritual music and lend cultural luster to an age of peace. Cai Jing championed Wei Hanjin's theories, rejected the stacked-millet method of earlier Confucian scholars, invoked the tradition that Yu of Xia used the human body as a standard of measure, took the emperor's finger as the pitch reference, and had the Imperial Cauldron and Splendid Bell cast.

sentences.zh: 樂成，賜名大晟，謂之雅樂，頒之天下，播之教坊，故崇寧以來有魏漢津樂。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, it was granted the name Great Flourishing, called elegant music, promulgated throughout the realm, and disseminated to the Music Office; hence from Chongning onward there was the music of Wei Hanjin.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was completed, it received the name Great Flourishing, was designated ceremonial music, promulgated throughout the empire, and disseminated to the palace Music Office—giving rise from the Chongning era onward to what was called Wei Hanjin's music.

sentences.zh: 夫韶、濩之音，下逮戰國，歷千數百年，猶能使人感嘆作興。

translations.literal: As for the tones of Shao and Hu, extending down to the Warring States period, through a thousand and several hundred years they could still make people sigh and be stirred to action.
translations.idiomatic: The music of Shao and Hu survived down to the Warring States era, and even after more than a thousand years could still move listeners to sigh and be stirred to action.

sentences.zh: 當是時，桑間、濮上之音已作，而古帝王之樂猶存，豈不以其制作有一定之器，而授受繼承亦代有其人歟？

translations.literal: At that time the music of Sangjian and Poshang had already arisen, yet the music of the ancient emperors and kings still survived—is this not because their production had fixed instruments, and transmission and succession also had their men in each generation?
translations.idiomatic: By then the decadent tunes of Sangjian and Poshang had already emerged, yet the music of the ancient sage-kings still survived. Was this not because their instruments were made to fixed standards, and each generation had specialists to transmit and preserve the tradition?

sentences.zh: 由是論之，鄭?、風雅不異器也。

translations.literal: Judging from this, Zheng and Wei music and the Feng and Ya pieces did not differ in instruments.
translations.idiomatic: From this perspective, the licentious music of Zheng and Wei and the court hymns of the Feng and Ya used the same instruments.

sentences.zh: 知此道也，則雖百世不易可也。

translations.literal: If one knows this Way, then even through a hundred generations it need not change.
translations.idiomatic: Once this principle is understood, the tradition can remain unchanged for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 禮樂道喪久矣，故宋之樂屢變，而卒無一定不易之論。

translations.literal: The Way of ritual and music has long been lost; therefore the music of Song changed repeatedly, yet in the end there was no settled and unchanging doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of ritual and music had long been in decline, which is why Song music was revised again and again yet never achieved a settled, enduring standard.

sentences.zh: 考諸家之說，累黍既各執異論，而身為度之說尤為荒唐。

translations.literal: Examining the theories of the various schools, on the stacked-millet method each held a different view, while the theory of taking the body as measure was especially absurd.
translations.idiomatic: A survey of competing theories shows that scholars already disagreed on the stacked-millet method, while the notion of using the human body as a standard of measure was especially absurd.

sentences.zh: 方古制作，欲垂萬世，難哉！

translations.literal: Compared with the productions of antiquity that were meant to endure for ten thousand generations, how difficult it is!
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the musical institutions of antiquity meant to endure for ten thousand generations, how difficult the task is!

sentences.zh: 觀其高二律、下一律之說，雖賢者有所未知，直曰樂聲高下於歌聲，則童子可知矣；

translations.literal: Observing their theories of raising two tones and lowering one tone—even the worthy had points they did not understand; simply say that the pitch of instrumental music is high or low relative to the pitch of singing, and even a child can know it;
translations.idiomatic: Their theories of raising pitch two tones or lowering it one tone puzzled even the learned; yet the simple truth that instrumental pitch should match vocal pitch is something a child can grasp;

sentences.zh: 八音克諧之說，智者有所未諭，直以歌聲齊簫聲，以簫聲定十六聲而齊八器，則愚者可諭矣。

translations.literal: On the theory that the eight sounds achieve harmony, the wise had points they did not grasp; simply align the singing voice with the pipe sound, use the pipe sound to fix the sixteen tones and thereby align the eight instruments, and then even the dull can be instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Their abstruse theories of harmonizing the eight categories of instruments likewise baffled the wise; yet align the voice with the pipes, use the pipes to establish the sixteen tones and tune the eight instrument types accordingly, and even the unlearned can understand.

sentences.zh: 審乎此道，以之制作，器定聲應，自不奪倫，移宮換羽，特餘事耳。

translations.literal: If one examines this Way and uses it in production, once instruments are fixed the sounds respond, and of themselves they do not usurp proper order; shifting modes and changing scale degrees are merely secondary matters.
translations.idiomatic: Grasp this principle in making music: once instruments are properly calibrated, their tones will harmonize naturally without disrupting proper order; modulations and scale changes are secondary concerns.

sentences.zh: 去惉懘靡曼而歸之和平澹泊，大雅之音，不是過也。

translations.literal: Remove harsh, cloying, and decadent strains and return to peacefulness and simplicity; the tones of great elegance are nothing beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: Discard harsh, decadent, and overly ornate strains and return music to tranquility and restraint—the tones of great elegance are nothing more than this.

sentences.zh: 南渡之後，大抵皆用先朝之舊，未嘗有所改作。

translations.literal: After the crossing south of the Yangzi, for the most part they all used what was old from the former dynasty and never undertook any new production.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south of the Yangzi, it largely retained the music of the previous dynasty and attempted no further reforms.

sentences.zh: 其後諸儒朱熹、蔡元定輩出，乃相與講明古今制作之本原，以究其歸極，著為成書，理明義析，具有條制，粲然使人知禮樂之不難行也。

translations.literal: Afterward the Confucian scholars Zhu Xi, Cai Yuanding, and their fellows appeared; they together elucidated the origins of ancient and modern production, pursued their ultimate principles, and wrote them into completed books—principles clear, meanings analyzed, provided with regulations and systems, brilliantly making people know that ritual and music are not hard to put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Later, scholars such as Zhu Xi and Cai Yuanding emerged. Working together, they elucidated the foundations of musical institutions past and present, pursued their underlying principles, and committed their findings to authoritative treatises—clear in reasoning, precise in analysis, and complete with systematic regulations that demonstrated ritual and music were not impracticable ideals.

sentences.zh: 惜乎宋祚告終，天下未一，徒亦空言而已。

translations.literal: Alas, the fortune of Song came to an end, the realm was not unified, and these remained empty words alone.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the Song dynasty came to its end before the realm was reunified, and their work remained mere words on the page.

sentences.zh: 今集累朝制作損益因革、議論是非，悉著于編，俾來者有考焉。

translations.literal: Now the productions, additions and subtractions, reforms and changes, and debates of right and wrong from successive reigns are all collected in this compilation, so that those who come after may have material for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: This compilation gathers the musical reforms, revisions, and debates of right and wrong from successive reigns, so that future readers may study them.

sentences.zh: 為樂志。

translations.literal: This constitutes the Treatise on Music.
translations.idiomatic: This constitutes the Treatise on Music.

sentences.zh: 王者致治，有四達之道，其二曰樂，所以和民心而化天下也。

translations.literal: When a king brings about good government, there are four penetrating Ways, the second of which is music, whereby the people's hearts are harmonized and the realm is transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler achieves good government, there are four avenues of influence, the second of which is music—by which the people's hearts are harmonized and the realm is transformed.

sentences.zh: 歷代相因，咸有制作。

translations.literal: Dynasties in succession inherited one from another, and all had their productions.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty inherited and revised musical institutions, each producing its own ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 唐定樂令，惟著器服之名。

translations.literal: The Tang fixed music statutes, recording only the names of instruments and ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang codified music regulations that recorded chiefly the names of instruments and ceremonial attire.

sentences.zh: 後唐莊宗起於朔野，所好不過北鄙鄭、?而已，先王雅樂，殆將掃地。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang rose from the northern frontier; what he favored was nothing beyond the rustic Zheng and Wei music of the north, and the elegant music of the former kings was nearly swept clean from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, who rose from the northern frontier, favored nothing but the rustic Zheng and Wei tunes of the borderlands, and the ceremonial music of the former kings was nearly lost altogether.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，始詔定朝會樂章、二舞、鼓吹十二案。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, an edict was first issued to fix court-assembly music sections, the two dances, and the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion music.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era of Later Jin, the court first issued edicts fixing the music for court assemblies, the civil and military dances, and the twelve wind-and-percussion ensembles.

sentences.zh: 周世宗嘗觀樂縣，問工人，不能答。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Zhou once inspected the suspended musical instruments and questioned the craftsmen, but they could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou once inspected the suspended musical instruments and questioned the craftsmen, but they could not answer his questions.

sentences.zh: 由是患雅樂凌替，思得審音之士以考正之，乃詔翰林學士竇儼兼判太常寺，與樞密使王朴同詳定，朴作律準，編古今樂事為正樂。

translations.literal: Because of this he was troubled that elegant music was declining and replaced, and wished to obtain men skilled in examining pitch to investigate and correct it; he then ordered Hanlin academician Dou Yi concurrently to direct the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and together with Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu to examine and fix it in detail; Pu made pitch standards and compiled music affairs ancient and modern into Correct Music.
translations.idiomatic: Disturbed that ceremonial music was in decline, he sought experts in pitch regulation to restore it. He ordered Hanlin academician Dou Yi to oversee the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and work with Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu on a thorough review. Wang Pu devised pitch standards and compiled a treatise on music ancient and modern entitled Correct Music.

sentences.zh: 宋初，命儼仍兼太常。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, Yi was ordered still to hold his concurrent post at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, Dou Yi was ordered to retain his concurrent post at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年二月，儼上言曰：「三、五之興，禮樂不相沿襲。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jianlong, Yi submitted a memorial saying: "When the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors rose, ritual and music did not follow one another unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jianlong 1 (960), Dou Yi memorialized: "When the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors rose, ritual and music were not carried on unchanged.

sentences.zh: 洪惟聖宋，肇建皇極，一代之樂，宜乎立名。

translations.literal: Solemnly considering the sacred Song, which had founded the imperial apex, music for a new dynasty ought to be given names.
translations.idiomatic: Solemnly considering the sacred Song, which had founded the imperial apex, music for a new dynasty ought to receive proper names.

sentences.zh: 樂章固當易以新詞，式遵舊典。」

translations.literal: The music sections should indeed be replaced with new words while following the old canon."
translations.idiomatic: The music sections should be replaced with new words while following the old canon."

sentences.zh: 從之，因詔儼專其事。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved, and an edict ordered Yi to oversee the matter exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal and ordered Dou Yi to oversee the matter exclusively.

sentences.zh: 儼乃改周樂文舞崇德之舞為文德之舞，武舞象成之舞為武功之舞，改樂章十二「順」為十二「安」，蓋取「治世之音安以樂」之義。

translations.literal: Yi then changed the Zhou-period civil dance Cultivating Virtue to Cultivating Civil Virtue, the martial dance Image of Completion to Martial Achievement, and renamed the twelve music sections from "shun" to "an," taking the meaning of "the sound of a well-governed age is eased by music."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi then renamed the Zhou civil dance Cultivating Virtue as Cultivating Civil Virtue, the martial dance Image of Completion as Martial Achievement, and changed the twelve music sections from "shun" to "an," taking the sense that "the sound of a well-governed age is eased by music."

sentences.zh: 祭天為高安，祭地為靜安，宗廟為理安，天地、宗廟登歌為嘉安，皇帝臨軒為隆安，王公出入為正安，皇帝食飲為和安，皇帝受朝、皇后入宮為順安，皇太子軒縣出入為良安，正冬朝會為永安，郊廟俎豆入為豐安，祭享、酌獻、飲福、受胙為禧安，祭文宣王、武成王同用永安，籍田、先農用靜安。

translations.literal: For sacrificing to Heaven: High Peace; to Earth: Tranquil Peace; ancestral temples: Ordered Peace; elevation song at Heaven and Earth altars and ancestral temples: Fine Peace; emperor receiving audience at the hall: Grand Peace; princes and dukes entering and leaving: Correct Peace; emperor dining: Harmonious Peace; emperor receiving court and empress entering palace: Accordant Peace; crown prince's suspended ensemble entering and leaving: Good Peace; winter solstice court assembly: Eternal Peace; entering suburban altars and temples with offerings: Abundant Peace; sacrifice presentation, libation, drinking blessings, receiving sacrificial meat: Auspicious Peace; sacrificing to Confucius and King Wu of Zhou both use Eternal Peace; sacred field plowing and Progenitor of Agriculture: Tranquil Peace.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned High Peace for sacrifices to Heaven, Tranquil Peace for Earth, Ordered Peace for ancestral temples, Fine Peace for elevation song at Heaven and Earth altars and ancestral temples, Grand Peace when the emperor received audience at the hall, Correct Peace for princes and dukes entering and leaving, Harmonious Peace when the emperor dined, Accordant Peace when the emperor received court and the empress entered the palace, Good Peace for the crown prince's suspended ensemble, Eternal Peace for the winter solstice court assembly, Abundant Peace when offerings entered suburban altars and temples, Auspicious Peace for sacrifice presentation, libation, drinking blessings, and receiving sacrificial meat, Eternal Peace for sacrifices to Confucius and King Wu of Zhou, and Tranquil Peace for sacred field plowing and the Progenitor of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 五月，有司上言：「僖祖文獻皇帝室奏大善之舞，順祖惠元皇帝室奏大寧之舞，翼祖簡恭皇帝室奏大順之舞，宣祖昭武皇帝室奏大慶之舞。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month the responsible offices submitted a memorial: "In the shrine of Ancestor Xi, Emperor Wenxian, perform the dance of Great Goodness; in the shrine of Ancestor Shun, Emperor Huiyuan, perform the dance of Great Tranquility; in the shrine of Ancestor Yi, Emperor Jiangong, perform the dance of Great Accord; in the shrine of Ancestor Xuan, Emperor Zhaowu, perform the dance of Great Celebration."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the responsible offices memorialized: "In the shrine of Ancestor Xi, Emperor Wenxian, perform the Dance of Great Goodness; in the shrine of Ancestor Shun, Emperor Huiyuan, the Dance of Great Tranquility; in the shrine of Ancestor Yi, Emperor Jiangong, the Dance of Great Accord; and in the shrine of Ancestor Xuan, Emperor Zhaowu, the Dance of Great Celebration."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，翰林學士承旨陶穀等奉詔撰定祀感生帝之樂章、曲名，降神用大安，太尉行用保安，奠玉幣用慶安，司徒奉俎用咸安，酌獻用崇安，飲福用廣安，亞獻、終獻用文安，送神用普安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Tao Gu and others received an edict to draft the music sections and tune names for sacrificing to the Progenitor of Life: Great Peace for escorting down spirits, Secure Peace for the Grand Commandant's procession, Celebratory Peace for offering jade silks, Complete Peace for the Minister of Works presenting offerings, Reverent Peace for libation, Broad Peace for drinking blessings, Cultivated Peace for the second and final offerings, and Universal Peace for seeing off spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 1 (963), Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Tao Gu and others were ordered to draft the music sections and tune names for sacrificing to the Progenitor of Life: Great Peace for escorting down the spirits, Secure Peace for the Grand Commandant's procession, Celebratory Peace for offering jade silks, Harmonious Peace when the Minister over the Masses presented the sacrificial viands, Reverent Peace for libation, Broad Peace for drinking blessings, Cultivated Peace for the second and final offerings, and Universal Peace for seeing off the spirits.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，樂工未具，是歲秋，行郊享之禮，詔選開封府樂工八百三十人，權隸太常習鼓吹。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, music workers had not been fully assembled. That autumn the suburban sacrifice was performed, and an edict selected eight hundred thirty musicians from Kaifeng Prefecture to be temporarily assigned to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for training in wind-and-percussion music.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, musicians had not been fully assembled. That autumn, when the suburban sacrifice was performed, an edict selected eight hundred thirty musicians from Kaifeng Prefecture and temporarily assigned them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to train in wind-and-percussion music.

sentences.zh: 四年春，遣拾遺孫吉取成都孟昶偽宮縣至京師，太常官屬閱視，考其樂器，不協音律，命毀棄之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Remonstrance Official Sun Ji was sent to fetch the false palace suspended instruments of Meng Chang of Chengdu to the capital; officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices inspected them, tested their instruments, found them not consonant with pitch and mode, and ordered them destroyed and discarded.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, Remonstrance Official Sun Ji was dispatched to bring the ceremonial instruments from the former palace of Meng Chang of Chengdu to the capital. Officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices inspected them, found the instruments out of tune with proper pitch standards, and ordered them destroyed.

sentences.zh: 六月，判太常寺和峴言：「大樂署舊制，宮縣三十六虡設於庭，登歌兩架設於殿上。

translations.literal: In the sixth month He Xian, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, said: "Under the old regulations of the Great Music Office, the palace suspended set of thirty-six frames was set up in the courtyard, and the two elevation-song stands were set up on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month He Xian, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, reported: "Under the old regulations of the Great Music Office, thirty-six frames of palace suspended instruments were set up in the courtyard, with two elevation-song stands on the hall platform.

sentences.zh: 望詔有司別造，仍令徐州求泗濱石以充磬材。」

translations.literal: It is hoped that an edict will order the responsible offices to make them separately anew, and also order Xuzhou to seek Sibi stone from the Si River bank to serve as material for sounding-stones."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the responsible offices be ordered to manufacture new sets, and that Xuzhou be instructed to procure Sibi stone from the banks of the Si River for sounding-stones."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉開運末，禮樂之器淪陷，至是，始令有司復二舞、十二案之制。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Kaiyun era of Jin, the instruments of ritual and music had been lost; only now was the order first given for the responsible offices to restore the systems of the two dances and the twelve wind-and-percussion sets.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Later Jin Kaiyun era, the ritual instruments had been lost. Only now did the court order the responsible offices to restore the civil and military dances and the twelve wind-and-percussion ensembles.

sentences.zh: 二舞郎及引舞一百五十人，按視教坊、開封樂籍，選樂工子弟以備其列，冠服準舊制。

translations.literal: For the two dance companies and the lead dancers, one hundred fifty persons in all, they inspected the registers of the Music Office and Kaifeng musicians, selected sons and younger brothers of music workers to fill the ranks, and caps and robes followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: For the two dance companies and lead dancers—one hundred fifty persons in all—the court reviewed the registers of the Music Office and Kaifeng musicians, selected trainees from musician families to fill the ranks, and assigned caps and robes according to the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹十二案，其制：設氈牀十二，為熊羆騰倚之狀，以承其下；

translations.literal: For the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion music, the system was: twelve felt couches were set up, fashioned in the shapes of bears, panthers, and soaring beasts, to support them from below;
translations.idiomatic: The twelve wind-and-percussion ensembles were arranged as follows: twelve felt platforms shaped like bears, panthers, and soaring beasts served as their bases;

sentences.zh: 每案設大鼓、羽葆鼓、金錞各一，歌、簫、笳各二，凡九人，其冠服同引舞之制。

translations.literal: each set had one large drum, one plumed-canopy drum, and one metal chime, and two singers, two pipes, and two horns apiece—nine persons in all—and their caps and robes followed the same regulations as the lead dancers.
translations.idiomatic: each ensemble had one large drum, one plumed-canopy drum, and one metal chime, plus two singers, two pipes, and two horns—nine performers in all—with caps and robes matching those of the lead dancers.

sentences.zh: 十月，峴又言：「樂器中有叉手笛，樂工考驗，皆與雅音相應。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xian again said: "Among the instruments there is the crossed-hands flute; when music workers tested it, all accorded with elegant tones.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month He Xian reported again: "Among the instruments is the crossed-hands flute. When music workers tested it, the tones matched ceremonial pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 按唐呂才歌白雪之琴，馬滔進太一之樂，當時得與宮縣之籍。

translations.literal: According to the Tang, Lü Cai played the zither song White Snow, and Ma Tao presented the music of the Great Unity; at the time they were allowed to join the register of palace suspended instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tang, Lü Cai performed the zither piece "White Snow," and Ma Tao presented the music of the Great Unity; both were admitted to the register of palace ceremonial instruments.

sentences.zh: 况此笛足以協十二旋相之宮，亦可通八十四調，其制如雅笛而小，長九寸，與黃鍾管等。

translations.literal: Moreover this flute is sufficient to harmonize the twelve cyclically related modes and can also traverse the eighty-four modes; its form is like the elegant flute but smaller, nine inches long, equal to the huangzhong pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this flute can harmonize the twelve cyclically related modes and traverse all eighty-four tonal configurations. It resembles the ceremonial flute but is smaller—nine inches long, matching the length of the huangzhong pitch pipe.

sentences.zh: 其竅有六，左四右二，樂人執持，兩手相交，有拱揖之狀，請名之曰『拱宸管』。

translations.literal: It has six holes, four on the left and two on the right; when music workers hold it, the two hands cross, showing the posture of arching and bowing; it is requested that it be named the "Arching-to-the-Sovereign Pipe."
translations.idiomatic: It has six finger holes—four on the left and two on the right. When held, the player's crossed hands resemble a bowing posture. He requested that it be named the "Arching-to-the-Sovereign Pipe."

sentences.zh: 望於十二案、十二編磬，登歌兩架各設其一，編於令式。」

translations.literal: It is hoped that on each of the twelve wind-and-percussion sets, the twelve sets of chime-stones, and the two elevation-song stands one each will be installed, and this be entered in the statutes and regulations."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that one be placed on each of the twelve wind-and-percussion ensembles, the twelve chime-stone sets, and the two elevation-song stands, and that this be codified in the music regulations."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 太祖每謂雅樂聲高，近於哀思，不合中和。

translations.literal: Taizu often said that the pitch of elegant music was high, close to mournful longing, and did not accord with central harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu often remarked that ceremonial music was pitched too high, sounding mournful rather than harmoniously balanced.

sentences.zh: 又念王朴、竇儼素名知樂，皆已淪沒，因詔峴討論其理。

translations.literal: He also recalled that Wang Pu and Dou Yi had long been famed for understanding music, but both had already perished; he therefore ordered Xian to investigate and discuss the principles.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Wang Pu and Dou Yi, both renowned for musical expertise, had died, and therefore ordered He Xian to investigate the underlying principles.

sentences.zh: 峴言：「以朴所定律呂之尺較西京銅望臬古制石尺短四分，樂聲之高，良由於此。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "Using the foot-measure by which Pu fixed the pitch pipes and comparing it with the ancient-regulation stone foot-measure of the bronze pitch tube at the Western Capital, it is four tenths shorter; the high pitch of the music is truly due to this."
translations.idiomatic: He Xian reported: "Wang Pu's pitch-measuring foot, compared with the ancient stone standard associated with the bronze pitch tube at the Western Capital, is four tenths shorter. This is precisely why the music sounds too high."

sentences.zh: 乃詔依古法別創新尺，以定律呂。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued to follow the ancient method and separately create a new foot-measure, thereby fixing the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed, ordering a new measuring foot to be devised according to ancient methods and used to regulate the pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 自此雅音和暢，事具律歷志。

translations.literal: From this time the elegant tones were harmonious and flowing; the matter is fully recorded in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and Calendars.
translations.idiomatic: From that point ceremonial music sounded harmonious and flowing; the details are recorded in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and Calendars.

sentences.zh: 自國初已來，御正殿受朝賀，用宮縣；

translations.literal: From the beginning of the dynasty onward, when holding court in the main hall to receive congratulatory audiences, the palace suspended set was used;
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the dynasty, audiences held in the main hall used the full palace suspended ensemble;

sentences.zh: 次御別殿，羣臣上壽，舉教坊樂。

translations.literal: next, when proceeding to a side hall, the assembled ministers offered longevity wishes, and the Music Office music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor then moved to a side hall for ministers to offer birthday felicitations, the palace Music Office ensemble performed.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬至，上御乾元殿受賀畢，羣臣詣大明殿行上壽禮，始用雅樂、登歌、二舞。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice, after the emperor had received congratulations in the Qianyuan Hall, the assembled ministers went to the Daming Hall to perform the longevity-wish rite, and for the first time elegant music, elevation song, and the two dances were used.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice, after receiving congratulations in the Qianyuan Hall, the emperor proceeded to the Daming Hall where ministers offered birthday felicitations. For the first time, ceremonial music, elevation song, and the civil and military dances were performed.

sentences.zh: 是月，和峴又上言：

translations.literal: That month He Xian again submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: That month He Xian submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 郊廟殿庭通用文德、武功之舞，然其綴兆未稱武功、文德之形容。

translations.literal: At suburban altars, temples, and palace halls the dances of Civil Virtue and Military Achievement were used in common, yet their choreography did not match the bearing of Military Achievement and Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban altars, temples, and palace halls all used the Civil Virtue and Military Achievement dances, yet their choreography did not reflect the true character of civil and military virtue.

sentences.zh: 又依古義，以揖讓得天下者，先奏文舞；

translations.literal: Moreover, according to ancient meaning, one who obtained the realm through yielding and deferring should first perform the civil dance;
translations.idiomatic: According to ancient precedent, a ruler who gained the realm through peaceful succession should perform the civil dance first;

sentences.zh: 以征伐得天下者，先奏武舞。

translations.literal: one who obtained the realm through campaigns and conquest should first perform the military dance.
translations.idiomatic: while one who gained it through military conquest should perform the military dance first.

sentences.zh: 陛下以推讓受禪，宜先奏文舞。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the abdication through yielding and deferring and ought first to perform the civil dance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the throne through peaceful abdication and should therefore perform the civil dance first.

sentences.zh: 按尚書，舜受堯禪，玄德升聞，乃命以位。

translations.literal: According to the Documents, when Shun received Yao's abdication, his deep virtue rose and was heard, and only then was he commanded to take the position.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Documents, when Shun received Yao's abdication, his deep virtue rose and was heard, and only then was he commanded to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 請改殿宇所用文舞為玄德升聞之舞。

translations.literal: It is requested that the civil dance used in palace halls be changed to the dance of Deep Virtue Rising and Heard.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the civil dance used in palace halls be renamed the Dance of Deep Virtue Rising and Heard.

sentences.zh: 其舞人，約唐太宗舞圖，用一百二十八人，以倍八佾之數，分為八行，行十六人，皆著履，執拂，服襜褶，冠進賢冠。

translations.literal: Its dancers, roughly following the dance diagram of Emperor Taizong of Tang, numbered one hundred twenty-eight persons, doubling the eight rows of eight dancers each, divided into eight rows of sixteen persons each; all wore shoes, held whisks, wore chanzhe pleated robes, and crowned themselves with the forward-worthy cap.
translations.idiomatic: The dancers, following roughly the choreography recorded for Emperor Taizong of Tang, numbered one hundred twenty-eight—twice the standard eight-by-eight formation—arranged in eight rows of sixteen. All wore shoes, carried ceremonial whisks, dressed in chanzhe pleated robes, and wore the forward-worthy cap.

sentences.zh: 引舞二人，各執五采纛，其舞狀、文容、變數，聊更增改。

translations.literal: Two lead dancers, each holding a five-colored banner, had their dance postures, civil bearing, and number of changes somewhat further increased and revised.
translations.idiomatic: Two lead dancers, each bearing a five-colored banner, had their movements, civil demeanor, and number of choreographic changes revised accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又陛下以神武平一宇內，即當次奏武舞。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty by divine martial prowess pacified all within the four seas, and therefore the military dance should be performed next.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty by divine martial prowess unified the realm, and the military dance should therefore follow.

sentences.zh: 按尚書，周武王一戎衣而天下大定，請改為天下大定之舞，其舞人數、行列，悉同文舞，其人皆被金甲持戟。

translations.literal: According to the Documents, King Wu of Zhou with one suit of armor brought great peace to the realm; it is requested that it be changed to the dance of Great Peace Throughout the Realm. Its number of dancers and rows were all the same as the civil dance, but the dancers all wore golden armor and held halberds.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Documents, King Wu of Zhou with a single suit of armor brought the realm to great peace. He requested that the military dance be renamed the Dance of Great Peace Throughout the Realm, with the same number and formation as the civil dance, but with all dancers clad in golden armor and bearing halberds.

sentences.zh: 引舞二人，各執五采旗。

translations.literal: Two lead dancers, each holding a five-colored flag.
translations.idiomatic: Two lead dancers, each carrying a five-colored flag.

sentences.zh: 其舞六變：一變象六師初舉，二變象上黨克平，三變象維揚底定，四變象荊湖歸復，五變象邛蜀納款，六變象兵還振旅。

translations.literal: Its dance had six changes: the first change symbolized the six armies first setting out; the second change symbolized the pacification of Shangdang; the third change symbolized the settling of Weiyang; the fourth change symbolized the recovery of Jinghu; the fifth change symbolized Qiong and Shu submitting allegiance; the sixth change symbolized the army returning and the troops being rallied.
translations.idiomatic: The dance had six choreographic changes: the first represented the six armies setting out; the second, the pacification of Shangdang; the third, the securing of the Huai region; the fourth, the recovery of Jinghu; the fifth, the submission of Qiong and Shu; and the sixth, the army's triumphant return.

sentences.zh: 乃別撰舞曲、樂章。

translations.literal: Thereupon dance tunes and music sections were separately composed.
translations.idiomatic: New dance melodies and musical sections were then composed for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 其鐃、鐸、雅、相、金錞、鼗鼓、引二舞等工人冠服，即依樂令，而文德、武功之舞，請於郊廟仍舊通用。

translations.literal: For the nao, duo, ya, xiang, metal chun, tao drums, and the lead dancers of the two dances and other performers, caps and robes followed the music statutes; but for the dances of Civil Virtue and Military Achievement, it is requested that at suburban altars and temples the old usage in common still be applied.
translations.idiomatic: The caps and robes of performers on the nao, duo, ya, xiang, metal chun, tao drums, and of the lead dancers followed the music statutes. For the suburban altars and temples, however, he requested that the old Civil Virtue and Military Achievement dances continue in use.

sentences.zh: 又按唐貞觀十四年，景雲見，河水清，張文收採古朱鴈、天馬之義，作景雲河清歌，名燕樂，元會第二奏者是也。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the Tang, in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan auspicious clouds appeared and the Yellow River ran clear; Zhang Wenshou adopted the meanings of the ancient Red Goose and Heavenly Horse and composed the song Auspicious Clouds and the River Clear, named Banquet Music, which was the second piece performed at the New Year's audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tang, in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, auspicious clouds appeared and the Yellow River ran clear. Zhang Wenshou drew on the ancient symbolism of the Red Goose and Heavenly Horse to compose "Auspicious Clouds and the River Clear," designated Banquet Music—the second piece performed at the New Year's audience.

sentences.zh: 伏見今年荊南進甘露，京兆、果州進嘉禾，黃州進紫芝，和州進綠毛龜，黃州進白兔。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that this year Jingnan presented sweet dew; Jingzhao and Guozhou presented fine grain; Huangzhou presented purple fungus; Hezhou presented a green-haired tortoise; and Huangzhou presented a white hare.
translations.idiomatic: This year Jingnan presented sweet dew; Jingzhao and Guozhou presented exceptional grain; Huangzhou presented purple fungus; Hezhou presented a green-haired tortoise; and Huangzhou presented a white hare.

sentences.zh: 欲依月律，撰神龜、甘露、紫芝、嘉禾、玉兔五瑞各一曲，每朝會登歌首奏之。

translations.literal: It is desired, following the monthly pitch modes, to compose one tune each for the five auspicious signs of the Divine Tortoise, Sweet Dew, Purple Fungus, Fine Grain, and Jade Hare, and at each court assembly have them performed first in the elevation song.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed composing one tune for each of the five auspicious omens—the Divine Tortoise, Sweet Dew, Purple Fungus, Fine Grain, and Jade Hare—according to the monthly pitch modes, to be performed first in the elevation song at each court assembly.

sentences.zh: 有詔：「二舞人數衣冠悉仍舊制，樂章如所請。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The numbers and caps and robes of the two dances shall all follow the old regulations; the music sections are as requested."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The numbers and attire of the two dances shall follow the old regulations; the musical sections are approved as requested."

sentences.zh: 六年，峴又言：「漢朝獲天馬、赤鴈、神鼎、白麟之瑞，並為郊歌。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Xian again said: "The Han dynasty obtained the auspicious signs of the Heavenly Horse, Red Wild Goose, Divine Cauldron, and White Unicorn, and all were made suburban hymns.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year He Xian reported again: "The Han dynasty, upon receiving the auspicious signs of the Heavenly Horse, Red Wild Goose, Divine Cauldron, and White Unicorn, composed suburban hymns for each.

sentences.zh: 國朝，合州進瑞木成文，馴象由遠方自至，秦州獲白烏，黃州獲白雀，並合播在筦絃，薦于郊廟。」

translations.literal: In our dynasty Hezhou presented auspicious wood with patterned grain, a tame elephant came of itself from a distant region, Qinzhou obtained a white crow, and Huangzhou obtained a white sparrow; all should together be disseminated on pipes and strings and presented at suburban altars and temples."
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, Hezhou presented patterned auspicious wood, a tame elephant arrived unbidden from afar, Qinzhou captured a white crow, and Huangzhou a white sparrow. He proposed setting all four to music and presenting them at the suburban altars and temples."

sentences.zh: 詔峴作瑞文、馴象、玉烏、皓雀四瑞樂章，以備登歌。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xian to compose four auspicious music sections—Auspicious Pattern, Tame Elephant, Jade Crow, and Bright Sparrow—to supplement the elevation song.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered He Xian to compose four auspicious musical sections—Auspicious Pattern, Tame Elephant, Jade Crow, and Bright Sparrow—for use in the elevation song.

sentences.zh: 未幾，峴復言：「按開元禮，郊祀，車駕還宮入嘉德門，奏采茨之樂；

translations.literal: Before long Xian again said: "According to the Kaiyuan Rites, at suburban sacrifice when the imperial carriage returned to the palace and entered the Gate of Excellent Virtue, the music Gathering Mulberry was performed;
translations.idiomatic: Before long He Xian reported again: "According to the Kaiyuan Rites, after a suburban sacrifice, when the imperial procession returned to the palace and entered the Gate of Excellent Virtue, the music Gathering Mulberry was performed;

sentences.zh: 入太極門，奏太和之樂。

translations.literal: upon entering the Gate of Supreme Ultimate, the music Supreme Harmony was performed.
translations.idiomatic: upon entering the Gate of Supreme Ultimate, the music Supreme Harmony was performed.

sentences.zh: 今郊祀禮畢，登樓肆赦，然後還宮，宮縣但用隆安，不用采茨。

translations.literal: Now when the suburban sacrifice rite is completed, the emperor ascends the tower and proclaims amnesty, and only afterward returns to the palace; the palace suspended set uses only Grand Peace and does not use Gathering Mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Today, after the suburban sacrifice, the emperor ascends the tower to proclaim amnesty and only then returns to the palace. The palace ensemble plays only Grand Peace and omits Gathering Mulberry.

sentences.zh: 其隆安樂章本是御殿之辭，伏詳禮意，隆安之樂自內而出，采茨之樂自外而入，若不並用，有失舊典。

translations.literal: The music section of Grand Peace was originally the text for the imperial hall; I humbly examine the ritual meaning: the music of Grand Peace proceeds from within, while the music of Gathering Mulberry proceeds from without; if both are not used together, the old canon is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Peace section was originally composed for audiences in the imperial hall. According to ritual propriety, Grand Peace represents music proceeding from within the palace, while Gathering Mulberry represents music entering from without. To omit either violates ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 今大樂署丞王光裕誦得唐日采茨曲，望依月律別撰其辭，每郊祀畢車駕初入，奏之。

translations.literal: Now Vice Director of the Great Music Office Wang Guangyu recited the Tang-period tune Gathering Mulberry; it is hoped that, following the monthly pitch modes, new text be separately composed, and that each time the suburban sacrifice is completed and the imperial carriage first enters, it be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Guangyu of the Great Music Office has recovered the Tang-period tune Gathering Mulberry. He requested that new lyrics be composed according to the monthly pitch modes and performed whenever the imperial procession first enters the palace after a suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 御樓禮畢還宮，即奏隆安之樂。」

translations.literal: When the rite on the imperial tower is completed and the emperor returns to the palace, Grand Peace is then performed."
translations.idiomatic: When the tower ceremony is complete and the emperor returns to the palace, Grand Peace should then be performed."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: All proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 太常寺又言：「準令，宗廟殿庭宮縣三十虡，郊社二十虡，殿庭加鼓吹十二案。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices again said: "According to the statutes, at ancestral temples and palace halls the palace suspended set has thirty frames; at suburban altars to Heaven and Earth it has twenty frames; at palace halls the twelve wind-and-percussion sets are added.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "According to statute, ancestral temples and palace halls require thirty frames of suspended instruments; suburban altars to Heaven and Earth require twenty; and palace halls add the twelve wind-and-percussion ensembles.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，郊祀誤用宗廟之數，今歲親郊，欲用舊禮。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, at suburban sacrifice the number for ancestral temples was mistakenly used; this year, for the emperor's personal suburban sacrifice, it is desired to use the old rites."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao, the suburban sacrifice mistakenly used the ancestral-temple complement. For this year's imperial suburban sacrifice, we wish to follow the correct precedent."

sentences.zh: 有詔，圜丘增十六虡，餘依前制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that for the Circular Mound Altar sixteen frames be added, and the rest follow the previous regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered sixteen additional frames for the Circular Mound Altar, with all else following established regulations.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國二年，冬至上壽，復用教坊樂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, at the winter-solstice longevity rite, the Music Office music was again used.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Emperor Taizong's winter-solstice longevity ceremony again employed Music Office ensembles.

sentences.zh: 九年，嵐州獻祥麟；

translations.literal: In the ninth year Lanzhou presented an auspicious unicorn;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Lanzhou presented an auspicious unicorn;

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，蘇州貢白龜；

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era Suzhou presented a white tortoise;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era Suzhou presented a white tortoise;

sentences.zh: 端拱初，澶州河清，廣州鳳凰集；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duan Gong era the Yellow River ran clear at Danzhou, and phoenixes gathered at Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Duan Gong era the Yellow River ran clear at Danzhou, and phoenixes gathered at Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 諸州麥兩穗、三穗者，連歲來上。

translations.literal: From various prefectures wheat with two ears or three ears on a stalk was presented year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year, various prefectures presented wheat stalks bearing two or three ears.

sentences.zh: 有司請以此五端為祥麟、丹鳳、河清、白龜、瑞麥之曲，薦于朝會，從之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested that these five auspicious signs be made into tunes for the Auspicious Unicorn, Cinnabar Phoenix, River Clear, White Tortoise, and Auspicious Wheat, to be presented at court assemblies; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed composing tunes for the five omens—the Auspicious Unicorn, Cinnabar Phoenix, River Clear, White Tortoise, and Auspicious Wheat—to be performed at court assemblies. The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，太子中允、直集賢院和㠓上言：「兄峴嘗於乾德中約唐志故事，請改殿庭二舞之名，舞有六變之象，每變各有樂章，歌詠太祖功業。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, He Meng, Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent and direct appointee to the Hall for Assembling Worthies, submitted a memorial: "My elder brother Xian once, in the Qiande era, followed Tang historical records and requested changing the names of the two hall dances; the dance has the symbolism of six changes, each change having its own music section singing of Taizu's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, He Meng of the Heir Apparent's staff and the Hall for Assembling Worthies memorialized: "My elder brother He Xian, during the Qiande era, followed Tang precedents in petitioning to rename the two hall dances. Each of the dance's six choreographic changes had its own musical section celebrating Emperor Taizu's achievements.

sentences.zh: 今詳來歲正會之儀，登歌五瑞之曲已從改製，則文武二舞亦當定其名。

translations.literal: Now, examining the ceremony for next year's New Year's audience, the elevation-song tunes of the five auspicious signs have already been reformed, so the civil and military dances should also have their names fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Now, for next year's New Year's audience, the elevation-song tunes for the five auspicious omens have already been revised; the civil and military dances should likewise receive definitive names.

sentences.zh: 周易有『化成天下』之辭，謂文德也；

translations.literal: The Changes has the phrase "transforming and completing the realm," which refers to civil virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes speaks of "transforming and completing the realm," referring to civil virtue;

sentences.zh: 漢史有『威加海內』之歌，謂武功也。

translations.literal: Han histories have the song "awe extending across the seas," which refers to military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Han histories record the song "awe extending across the seas," referring to military achievement.

sentences.zh: 望改殿庭舊用玄德升聞之舞為化成天下之舞，天下大定之舞為威加海內之舞。

translations.literal: It is requested that the civil dance formerly used in palace halls, Deep Virtue Rising and Heard, be changed to the dance of Transforming and Completing the Realm, and the dance of Great Peace Throughout the Realm be changed to the dance of Awe Extending Across the Seas.
translations.idiomatic: He requested renaming the civil dance Deep Virtue Rising and Heard to Transforming and Completing the Realm, and the military dance Great Peace Throughout the Realm to Awe Extending Across the Seas.

sentences.zh: 其舞六變：一變象登臺講武，二變象漳、泉奉土，三變象杭、越來朝，四變象克殄?、汾，五變象肅清銀、夏，六變象兵還振旅。

translations.literal: Its dance had six changes: the first change symbolized mounting the terrace to review troops; the second change symbolized Zhang and Quan submitting their territories; the third change symbolized Hang and Yue coming to court; the fourth change symbolized the extermination of Bing and Fen; the fifth change symbolized the pacification of Yin and Xia; the sixth change symbolized the army returning and troops being rallied.
translations.idiomatic: The military dance had six choreographic changes: the first represented reviewing troops upon the terrace; the second, Zhang and Quan submitting their territories; the third, Hang and Yue coming to court; the fourth, the conquest of Bing and Fen; the fifth, the pacification of Yin and Xia; and the sixth, the army's triumphant return.

sentences.zh: 每變樂章各一首。」

translations.literal: Each change had one music section."
translations.idiomatic: Each change had its own musical section."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 三年，元日朝賀畢，再御朝元殿，羣臣上壽，復用宮縣、二舞，登歌五瑞曲，自此遂為定制。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the New Year's congratulatory audience was completed, the emperor again proceeded to the Chaoyuan Hall, the assembled ministers offered longevity wishes, and the palace suspended set, two dances, and elevation-song tunes of the five auspicious signs were again used; from this time it became a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after the New Year's audience, the emperor proceeded to the Chaoyuan Hall where ministers offered birthday felicitations. The full palace ensemble, civil and military dances, and the five auspicious elevation-song tunes were restored, establishing a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 㠓又請取今朝祥瑞之殊尤者作為四瑞樂章，備郊廟奠獻，以代舊曲，詔從之。

translations.literal: Meng again requested that the most outstanding auspicious signs of the present court be made into four auspicious music sections to supplement suburban altar and temple offerings, replacing the old tunes; an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: He Meng further proposed composing four auspicious musical sections from the most remarkable omens of the current reign for suburban altar and temple offerings, replacing older tunes. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 有司雖承詔，不能奉行，故今闕其曲。

translations.literal: Although the responsible offices received the edict, they could not carry it out, and therefore the tunes are now missing.
translations.idiomatic: Although the responsible offices received the edict, they failed to implement it, and the tunes are therefore lost.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂舜作五絃之琴以歌南風，後王因之，復加文武二絃。

translations.literal: Taizong once said that Shun made the five-string zither to sing the Southern Winds, and later kings followed this, adding two more strings for civil and military virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once observed that Shun created the five-string zither to perform the Southern Winds, and later rulers added two strings representing civil and military virtue.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，乃增作九絃琴、五絃阮，別造新譜三十七卷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, nine-string zithers and five-string ruan lutes were additionally made, and thirty-seven volumes of new scores were separately composed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao, the court introduced nine-string zithers and five-string ruan lutes and composed thirty-seven volumes of new musical scores.

sentences.zh: 凡造九絃琴宮調、鳳吟商調、角調、徵調、羽調、龍仙羽調、側蜀調、黃鍾調、無射商調、瑟調變弦法各一。

translations.literal: In all, for the nine-string zither one method each was made for palace mode, Phoenix-Song shang mode, jue mode, zhi mode, yu mode, Dragon-Immortal yu mode, lateral Shu mode, huangzhong mode, wuye shang mode, and se-mode string-changing.
translations.idiomatic: For the nine-string zither, a distinct string-tuning method was devised for each mode: palace, Phoenix-Song shang, jue, zhi, yu, Dragon-Immortal yu, lateral Shu, huangzhong, wuye shang, and se-mode variation.

sentences.zh: 制宮調鶴唳天弄、鳳吟商調鳳來儀弄、龍仙羽調八仙操，凡三曲。

translations.literal: Composed were palace-mode Crane Cries to Heaven, Phoenix-Song shang-mode Phoenix Comes with Rites, and Dragon-Immortal yu-mode Eight Immortals Suite—three pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: Three new compositions were created: Crane Cries to Heaven in palace mode, Phoenix Comes with Rites in Phoenix-Song shang mode, and Eight Immortals Suite in Dragon-Immortal yu mode.

sentences.zh: 又以新聲被舊曲者，宮調四十三曲，商調十三曲，角調二十三曲，徵調十四曲，羽調二十六曲，側蜀調四曲，黃鍾調十九曲，無射商調七曲，瑟調七曲。

translations.literal: Old tunes overlaid with new sounds numbered: palace mode forty-three pieces, shang mode thirteen, jue mode twenty-three, zhi mode fourteen, yu mode twenty-six, lateral Shu mode four, huangzhong mode nineteen, wuye shang mode seven, and se mode seven.
translations.idiomatic: Existing tunes were adapted with new sounds: forty-three in palace mode, thirteen in shang, twenty-three in jue, fourteen in zhi, twenty-six in yu, four in lateral Shu, nineteen in huangzhong, seven in wuye shang, and seven in se mode.

sentences.zh: 造五弦阮宮調、商調、鳳吟商調鳳吟商調 「商」字原脫，據宋會要樂四之一四補、

translations.literal: For the five-string ruan, palace mode, shang mode, and Phoenix-Song shang mode were made—the character "shang" was originally missing and has been supplied according to Song Huiyao, Music 4.1.4.
translations.idiomatic: For the five-string ruan, tuning methods were devised for palace mode, shang mode, and Phoenix-Song shang mode (the character "shang" was originally missing and has been restored per Song Huiyao, Music 4.1.4).

sentences.zh: 角調、徵調、羽調、黃鍾調、無射商調、瑟調、碧玉調、慢角調、金羽調變弦法各一金羽調變弦法各一 「各一」二字原脫，據宋會要樂四之一四補。。

translations.literal: jue mode, zhi mode, yu mode, huangzhong mode, wuye shang mode, se mode, jade-green mode, slow jue mode, and golden yu mode—one string-changing method for each; the two characters "one each" for golden yu mode were originally missing and have been supplied according to Song Huiyao, Music 4.1.4.
translations.idiomatic: Jue, zhi, yu, huangzhong, wuye shang, se, jade-green, slow jue, and golden yu modes—each with its own string-tuning method (the words "one each" were originally missing and have been restored per Song Huiyao, Music 4.1.4).

sentences.zh: 制宮調鶴唳天弄、鳳吟商調鳳來儀弄，凡二曲。

translations.literal: Composed were palace-mode Crane Cries to Heaven and Phoenix-Song shang-mode Phoenix Comes with Rites—two pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: Two new ruan compositions were created: Crane Cries to Heaven in palace mode and Phoenix Comes with Rites in Phoenix-Song shang mode.

sentences.zh: 又以新聲被舊曲者，宮調四十四曲、商調十三曲、角調十一曲、徵調十曲、羽調十曲、黃鍾調黃鍾調 「調」字原脫，據宋會要樂四之一四補。

translations.literal: Old tunes overlaid with new sounds for the ruan numbered: palace mode forty-four pieces, shang thirteen, jue eleven, zhi ten, yu ten, and huangzhong mode—the character "mode" for huangzhong was originally missing and has been supplied according to Song Huiyao, Music 4.1.4.
translations.idiomatic: Adapted ruan tunes numbered forty-four in palace mode, thirteen in shang, eleven in jue, ten in zhi, ten in yu, and nineteen in huangzhong mode (the character "mode" for huangzhong was originally missing and has been restored per Song Huiyao, Music 4.1.4).

sentences.zh: 十九曲、無射商調七曲、瑟調七曲、碧玉調十四曲、慢角調十曲、金羽調三曲。

translations.literal: nineteen pieces, wuye shang mode seven pieces, se mode seven, jade-green mode fourteen, slow jue mode ten, and golden yu mode three.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen in huangzhong, seven in wuye shang, seven in se, fourteen in jade-green, ten in slow jue, and three in golden yu mode.

sentences.zh: 阮成，以示中書門下，因謂曰：「雅樂與鄭、?不同，鄭聲淫，非中和之道。

translations.literal: When the ruan was completed, it was shown to the Secretariat and Chancellery, and the emperor said: "Elegant music differs from Zheng and Wei music; Zheng sounds are licentious and are not the Way of central harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruan was completed, it was presented to the Secretariat. The emperor remarked: "Ceremonial music differs from the licentious music of Zheng and Wei. Zheng music is decadent and not the path of harmonious balance.

sentences.zh: 朕常思雅正之音可以治心，原古聖之旨，尚存遺美。

translations.literal: I have often thought that elegant and correct tones can govern the mind; tracing the intent of the ancient sages, their remaining beauties still survive.
translations.idiomatic: I have long believed that refined, correct music can cultivate the mind. Tracing the intent of the ancient sages, something of their musical legacy still survives.

sentences.zh: 琴七弦，朕今增之為九，其名曰君、臣、文、武、禮、樂、正、民、心，則九奏克諧而不亂矣。

translations.literal: The zither has seven strings; I have now increased them to nine, named Ruler, Minister, Civil, Military, Ritual, Music, Correctness, People, and Mind—then the nine performances achieve harmony without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The zither has seven strings; I have added two more to make nine, named Ruler, Minister, Civil, Military, Ritual, Music, Correctness, People, and Mind—so that nine performances may achieve harmony without disorder.

sentences.zh: 阮四絃，增之為五，其名曰：水、火、金、木、土，則五材並用而不悖矣。」

translations.literal: The ruan has four strings; I have increased them to five, named Water, Fire, Metal, Wood, and Earth—then the five materials are all employed without contradiction."
translations.idiomatic: The ruan has four strings; I have added a fifth, named Water, Fire, Metal, Wood, and Earth—so that the five elements may work together without conflict."

sentences.zh: 因命待詔朱文濟、蔡裔齎琴、阮詣中書彈新聲，詔宰相及近侍咸聽焉。

translations.literal: He then ordered awaiting-edict Zhu Wenji and Cai Yi to bring the zither and ruan to the Secretariat to perform the new music, and ordered the chief ministers and close attendants all to listen.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered awaiting-edict Zhu Wenji and Cai Yi to bring the instruments to the Secretariat to perform the new music, and commanded chief ministers and close attendants to attend.

sentences.zh: 由是中外獻賦頌者數十人。

translations.literal: Because of this, within and without the court several tens of persons presented fu and eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: In response, dozens of officials inside and outside the court submitted celebratory compositions.

sentences.zh: 二年，太常音律官田琮以九弦琴、五弦阮均配十二律，旋相為宮，隔八相生，並協律呂，冠于雅樂，仍具圖以獻。

translations.literal: In the second year Tian Cong, pitch-and-mode officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, matched the nine-string zither and five-string ruan evenly to the twelve pitch pipes, made them cyclically generate modes, generated tones across the eight-step interval, and all accorded with pitch pipes and modes, placing them at the head of elegant music; he also presented diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Tian Cong, a pitch specialist of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, demonstrated that the nine-string zither and five-string ruan could be tuned to all twelve pitch pipes, generate modes cyclically, and produce tones across the full scale in perfect accord with pitch standards. He ranked them foremost among ceremonial instruments and submitted explanatory diagrams.

sentences.zh: 上覽而嘉之，遷其職以賞焉。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed them and commended them, promoting his office as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed the submission with approval and promoted him as a reward.

sentences.zh: 自是遂廢拱宸管。

translations.literal: From this time the Arching-to-the-Sovereign Pipe was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Arching-to-the-Sovereign Pipe was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平四年，太常寺言：「樂工習藝匪精，每祭享郊廟，止奏黃鍾宮一調，未嘗隨月轉律，望示條約。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping under Emperor Zhenzong, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "Music workers' practice of their arts is not refined; at each suburban altar and temple sacrifice they perform only the huangzhong palace mode and have never shifted pitch according to the month; it is hoped that regulations be promulgated."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Musicians' training is inadequate. At suburban and temple sacrifices they perform only the huangzhong palace mode and never shift pitch according to the month. We request that regulations be issued."

sentences.zh: 乃命翰林侍讀學士夏侯嶠、判寺郭贊同按試，擇其曉習月律者，悉增月奉，自餘權停廩給，再俾學習，以奬勵之。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting Xia Houqiao and acting director Guo Zan jointly to examine and test them, select those who understood monthly pitch modes, increase all their monthly salaries, temporarily suspend grain rations for the rest, and have them study again, to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Hanlin academician Xia Houqiao and acting director Guo Zan to examine the musicians, increase the salaries of those proficient in monthly pitch regulation, suspend rations for the rest pending further training, and thereby encourage improvement.

sentences.zh: 雖頗振綱紀，然亦未能精備。

translations.literal: Although discipline was somewhat restored, it still could not be made fully refined.
translations.idiomatic: Although discipline improved somewhat, full proficiency was not achieved.

sentences.zh: 蓋樂工止以年勞次補，而不以藝進，至有抱其器而不能振作者，故難於驟變。

translations.literal: This was because music workers were appointed only by years of service and seniority, not advanced by artistry; there were even those who held their instruments yet could not perform—hence it was hard to change suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians were appointed by seniority rather than skill, and some could not even play their instruments competently—making rapid reform difficult.

sentences.zh: 景德二年八月，監察御史艾仲孺上言，請修飾樂器，調正音律，乃詔翰林學士李宗諤權判太常寺，及令內臣監修樂器。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Jingde, Investigating Censor Ai Zhongru submitted a memorial requesting repair of musical instruments and correction of pitch and mode; an edict then ordered Hanlin Academician Li Zong'e to act as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ordered inner palace personnel to supervise repair of instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Jingde, Investigating Censor Ai Zhongru petitioned to repair musical instruments and correct pitch standards. The court ordered Hanlin academician Li Zong'e to oversee the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and assigned inner-court personnel to supervise instrument repairs.

sentences.zh: 後復以龍圖閣待制戚綸同判寺事，乃命太樂、鼓吹兩署工校其優劣，黜去濫吹者五十餘人。

translations.literal: Later Qi Lun, Attendant Drafting Official of the Dragon Diagram Hall, was also made co-director of the court; they then ordered workers of the Great Music and Wind-and-Drum offices to compare their relative excellence and dismissed more than fifty who blew indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi Lun of the Dragon Diagram Hall was appointed co-director. Musicians of the Great Music and Wind-and-Drum offices were compared for competence, and more than fifty incompetent performers were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宗諤因編次律呂法度、樂物名數，目曰樂纂，又裁定兩署工人試補條式及肄習程課。

translations.literal: Li Zong'e thereupon compiled pitch-pipe methods and degrees, and the names and numbers of musical objects, entitling it Compendium of Music, and also fixed examination and appointment regulations and practice curricula for workers of the two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zong'e compiled pitch standards, instrument specifications, and nomenclature into a work entitled Compendium of Music, and established examination, appointment, and training regulations for both music offices.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，上御崇政殿張宮縣閱試，召宰執、親王臨觀，宗諤執樂譜立侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year the emperor proceeded to the Chongzheng Hall, set out the palace suspended set for review and testing, summoned chief ministers and imperial princes to observe, and Li Zong'e stood holding the score in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The following eighth month, the emperor held a review at the Chongzheng Hall with the palace suspended ensemble fully deployed, summoning chief ministers and imperial princes to observe while Li Zong'e stood by with the musical score.

sentences.zh: 先以鍾磬按律準，次令登歌，鍾、磬、塤、箎、琴、阮、笙、簫各二色合奏，箏、瑟、筑三色合奏，迭為一曲，復擊鎛鍾為六變、九變。

translations.literal: First bells and stones were tuned to the pitch standard; next elevation song was ordered; bells, stones, ocarina, bamboo flute, zither, ruan, sheng, and xiao—two of each type—performed together; zheng, se, and zhu—three types—performed together; they alternated as one piece; then the great bell was struck for six changes and nine changes.
translations.idiomatic: First the bells and stones were tuned to pitch standards, then the elevation song was performed. Bells, stones, ocarina, bamboo flute, zither, ruan, sheng, and xiao—two of each—played together, alternating with zheng, se, and zhu. The great bell was then struck through six and nine choreographic changes.

sentences.zh: 又為朝會上壽之樂及文武二舞、鼓吹、導引、警夜之曲，頗為精習。

translations.literal: Music for court assembly longevity rites, the civil and military dances, wind-and-percussion, procession, and night-watch pieces were also performed with considerable refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Music for court assemblies, birthday ceremonies, civil and military dances, wind-and-percussion, procession, and night-watch pieces was performed with considerable refinement.

sentences.zh: 上甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 舊制，巢笙、和笙每變宮之際，必換義管，然難於遽易，樂工單仲辛遂改為一定之制，不復旋易，與諸宮調皆協。

translations.literal: Under the old system, for nest-sheng and harmony-sheng, whenever the mode changed the auxiliary pipes had to be replaced, but this was hard to do quickly; music worker Shan Zhongxin therefore changed it to a fixed system, no longer rotating replacements, and it accorded with all modes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, nest-sheng and harmony-sheng required replacing auxiliary pipes whenever the mode changed—a cumbersome procedure. Musician Shan Zhongxin devised a fixed configuration that eliminated the need for rotation while harmonizing with all modes.

sentences.zh: 又令仲辛誕唱八十四調曲，遂詔補副樂正，賜袍笏、銀帶，自餘皆賜衣帶、緡錢，又賜宗諤等器幣有差。

translations.literal: He also had Zhongxin perform songs in all eighty-four modes; an edict then appointed him assistant director of music, bestowing robe, court tablet, and silver belt; the rest were all given robes, belts, and strings of cash; Li Zong'e and others were also given vessels and silks in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxin was commanded to perform songs in all eighty-four modes and appointed assistant director of music, receiving official robes, court tablet, and silver belt. Other musicians received robes, belts, and cash rewards, while Li Zong'e and others received gifts of vessels and silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 自是，樂府制度頗有倫理。

translations.literal: From this time the institutions of the Music Office had considerable order and principle.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Music Office operated with considerably greater order and coherence.

sentences.zh: 是，惟天地、感生帝、宗廟用樂，親祀用宮縣，有司攝事，止用登歌，自餘大祀，未暇備樂。

translations.literal: At this time, only Heaven and Earth, the Progenitor of Life, and the ancestral temples used music; when the emperor sacrificed in person the palace suspended set was used; when officials conducted the rite on his behalf only elevation song was used; for the remaining great sacrifices, there was no leisure to provide full music.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, music was provided only for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Progenitor of Life, and the ancestral temples. Imperial sacrifices in person used the full palace ensemble; when officials conducted rites on the emperor's behalf, only elevation song was performed. Other major sacrifices still lacked complete musical provision.

sentences.zh: 時既罷兵，垂意典禮，至是詔曰：「致恭明神，邦國之重事；

translations.literal: The time having ended warfare, the emperor turned his attention to canonical rites; thereupon an edict stated: "Showing reverence to the luminous spirits is a weighty affair of the state;
translations.idiomatic: With warfare concluded, the emperor turned his attention to ritual institutions. An edict declared: "Showing reverence to the luminous spirits is a weighty affair of state;

sentences.zh: 升薦備樂，方冊之彝章。

translations.literal: Offering ascent and presentation with complete music is the constant regulation of written codes.
translations.idiomatic: presenting offerings with full musical accompaniment is the constant regulation of written codes.

sentences.zh: 矧在尊神，固當嚴奉。

translations.literal: How much more for the honored spirits—surely they ought to be strictly served.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for the honored spirits, who surely deserve the strictest observance.

sentences.zh: 舉行舊典，用格明靈。

translations.literal: Uphold and perform the old canon to move the luminous spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold and perform the ancient canon to move the luminous spirits.

sentences.zh: 自今諸大祠並宜用樂，皆同感生帝，六變、八變如通禮所載。」

translations.literal: From now on all great sacrifices should use music, all the same as for the Progenitor of Life, with six changes and eight changes as recorded in the comprehensive rites."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all major sacrifices shall employ music, with six and eight choreographic changes as prescribed in the comprehensive rites, following the precedent of the Progenitor of Life."

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年四月，詳定所言：「東封道路稍遠，欲依故事，山上圜臺及山下封祀壇前俱設登歌兩架，壇下設二十架?二舞，其朝覲壇前亦設二十架，更不設熊羆十二案。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the review committee stated: "The eastern Feng and Shan journey is somewhat distant; it is desired, following precedent, to set up two elevation-song stands both at the circular altar on the mountain and before the Feng-sacrifice altar below the mountain, to set up twenty frames and the two dances below the altar, and also twenty frames before the audience altar, and no longer to set up the twelve bear-and-panther wind-and-percussion sets."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the review committee reported: "The eastern Feng and Shan journey is lengthy. Following precedent, we propose two elevation-song stands at both the mountaintop circular altar and the altar below, twenty frames of suspended instruments and the two dances at the base of the altar, twenty frames at the audience altar, and no bear-and-panther wind-and-percussion ensembles."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，都官員外郎、判太常禮院孫奭上言：「按禮文，饗太廟終獻降階之後，武舞止，太祝徹豆，豐安之樂作，一成止，然後理安之樂作，是謂送神。
